newsitem.title: ITALY: FORECAST-Italy PPI seen flat yr/yr in September.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Italy PPI seen flat yr/yr in September.

text.p: Italy's producer prices are seen rising slightly on a monthly basis in September but they should be steady year-on-year, a Reuter poll of analysts showed.
Analysts expect an average PPI rise of 0.15 percent on a monthly basis and a 0.04 percent increase yearly. September PPI and wholesale price data are due out on Monday morning.
In August, producer prices rose 0.1 pct on a monthly basis and were unchanged yearly at zero. In September 1995 they rose 0.1 pct monthly and 8.7 pct yearly.

Wholesale pricers are seen rising 0.27 pct monthly and 1.17 yearly. In August WPI rose 0.1 percent monthly and fell by 0.2 percent yearly. In September 1995 wholesale prices rose 1.1 percent monthly and 11.6 percent on a yearly basis.

Differences in analysts' forecasts of September PPI stem from a different interpretation of the impact of the recent price rise in the oil sector. In September, oil prices rose 10.9 percent on a monthly basis from a 4.0 percent rise in August.

"On a yearly basis, producer prices should show no change, but if you exclude the energy and food sectors they should fall by 0.8 percent. In August core prices fell by 0.6 percent" says Martino Dolfini, economist at Chase Manhattan Bank in Milan.
Other analysts says the rise in oil prices took place in the second half of September and therefore should not weigh too much on the basket.

"We should not overvalue the oil increase because it has been balanced by a fall in the prices of other raw materials" says Paolo Casadio, economist at Credito Italiano. "If there is an increase in producer prices, it will come from labour costs," he added.
